newsitem.title: UK: UK Labour ahead but pre-election poll lead slips.
newsitem.headline: UK Labour ahead but pre-election poll lead slips.

text.p: The opposition Labour party's lead over Britain's ruling Conservatives has slipped to 17 percent from 19 last month, an NOP poll in the Sunday Times said.

The poll showed support for Labour at 49 percent, down from 50 percent in December, compared with 32 percent for the Conservatives, up from 31 percent. The centre-left Liberal Democrats slipped to 13 percent from 14 percent.
The Sunday Times said the poll showed that Labour's lead was being squeezed, but only slowly.
Labour, which has been in opposition since 1979, was scoring well over 50 percent a year ago and has averaged 48 percent over the past four months.
The Conservatives, who enjoyed 25-26 percent support a year ago, have averaged 32 percent in the same period.
The paper said one glimmer of hope for Prime Minister John Major was that 30 percent of voters say they could still change their minds between now and the election, which must be held by May 22.

"Overall, however, there is little in the poll to encourage the Tories as the election draws near. Asked whether they felt better off than a year ago, only 18 percent said they did, against 32 percent who said they were worse off and 38 percent about the same," the Sunday Times said.
In a major reversal of the position before the last election in 1992, the poll showed that Labour was now trusted more than the Conservatives on the key election issue of taxation.
Of those surveyed, 53 percent expected higher taxes if the Conservatives won a fifth consecutive term in office, while 44 percent expected taxes to go up if Labour took power.
NOP interviewed 1,591 people face to face last Thursday.
